proposals.before: After Zhiyou capitulated, Qing absorbed his troops under the banner of the Qisheng Battalion and was promoted by recommendation to the rank of battalion commander.
proposals.after: After Zhiyou capitulated, Qing absorbed his troops under the banner of the Qisheng Battalion and was promoted by recommendation to the rank of qianzong (company officer).
proposals.reason: 千總 is a company-level officer rank, not a battalion commander.

proposals.before: When Zhiyou surrendered, [Qing] thereupon took over command of his forces, styled the camp Qisheng, and was recommended and appointed a battalion commander.
proposals.after: When Zhiyou surrendered, [Qing] thereupon took over command of his forces, styled the camp Qisheng, and was recommended and appointed a qianzong (company officer).
proposals.reason: Same error in the literal rendering of 千總 as battalion commander.

proposals.before: He was granted the second-class Order of the Chariot of War and appointed provincial military commander of Hunan.
proposals.after: He was granted the second-class Light Chariot Commandant (qingche duwei) and appointed provincial military commander of Hunan.
proposals.reason: 二等輕車都尉 is a Qing hereditary rank, not an Order of the Chariot of War.

proposals.before: He was granted the second-class Order of the Chariot of War and appointed Provincial Military Commander of Hunan.
proposals.after: He was granted the second-class Light Chariot Commandant (qingche duwei) and appointed Provincial Military Commander of Hunan.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 輕車都尉 in the literal field.

proposals.before: Qing was roughly the same age and rank as the other generals; suddenly placed over them, many resented his command, and the seventy-odd camps of allied forces fell into disorder.
proposals.after: Qing was roughly the same age and seniority as the other generals; suddenly placed over them, many resented his command, and the seventy-odd camps of allied forces fell into disorder.
proposals.reason: Chinese 行輩相若 denotes shared generational seniority among peers, not official rank; the idiomatic 'rank' misrenders 行輩.

proposals.before: When the Japanese crossed the Yalu, the Chinese were defeated and fell back toward Fengcheng, then made their stand on Dagao Ridge.
proposals.after: When the Japanese crossed the Yalu, the Chinese were defeated; the enemy pressed straight toward Fengcheng, and the Chinese fell back to hold Dagao Ridge.
proposals.reason: Chinese 直趨鳳凰城 is the Japanese advance on Fengcheng after the Qing defeat; 退扼大高嶺 is the Qing fallback. The idiomatic version wrongly has the Chinese falling back toward Fengcheng.

proposals.before: When eastern affairs began, Qing as Lüshun defender went to guard Jiuliancheng; Hongzhang separately ordered Jiang Guaiti and others to defend Lüshun, with Bangdao assisting.
proposals.after: When eastern affairs began, Qing as Lüshun defender went to guard Jiuliancheng; Li Hongzhang separately ordered Jiang Guaiti and others to defend Lüshun, with Bangdao assisting.
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the surname from 李鴻章, leaving ambiguous bare Hongzhang.

proposals.before: He entered service as a military student under Song Qing in campaigns against the Nian rebels, rose through merit to colonel, and received the Manchu honorific Zhenyong Batulu.
proposals.after: He entered service as a military student under Song Qing in campaigns against the Nian rebels, rose through merit to major, and received the Manchu honorific Zhenyong Batulu.
proposals.reason: 都司 ranks below 參將 (colonel in s0076); rendering 都司 as colonel conflates distinct Qing grades.

proposals.before: As a military student he followed Song Qing against the Nian, accumulated merit to colonel, and was granted the title Zhenyong Batulu.
proposals.after: As a military student he followed Song Qing against the Nian, accumulated merit to major, and was granted the title Zhenyong Batulu.
proposals.reason: Literal English also renders 都司 as colonel; the Qing grade is major, below 參將.

proposals.before: Before long the Japanese massed in great numbers; Qing fell into heavy encirclement, fell from his horse wounded, Yukun broke through the encirclement to enter, escorted him out on both sides, and casualties were exceptionally heavy.
proposals.after: Before long the Japanese massed in great numbers; Qing fell into heavy encirclement, fell from his horse wounded; Yukun broke through the encirclement to enter, shielded him and brought him out, and casualties were exceptionally heavy.
proposals.reason: 翼之出 means to shield/flank and escort him out; rendering 翼 as 'on both sides' misreads the verb.

proposals.before: At that time the Russians, because of disputes over revising the Ili treaty, had words of breach; the Uliastai consultant Xichang had long known I Ketang'a was versed in tactics and requested an edict to recruit hunters nearby to guard Hunchun.
proposals.after: At that time the Russians, over revision of the Ili treaty, raised objections; the Uliastai consultant Xichang had long known I Ketang'a was versed in tactics and requested an edict to recruit hunters nearby to guard Hunchun.
proposals.reason: 有違言 means there were objections or disputed words; 'had words of breach' is unnatural and obscures the sense.

proposals.before: In the twenty-fifth year he died; he was given the posthumous name Chengyong, Loyal and Brave, and a memorial temple.
proposals.after: In the twenty-fifth year he died; he was given the posthumous name Chengyong and a memorial temple was granted.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English inserts the glosses 'Loyal and Brave' as if part of the bestowed name; Chinese only gives 誠勇 and the temple grant.

proposals.before: Once he arrived, they deliberated to use attack as defense.
proposals.after: Once they arrived, they deliberated to use attack as defense.
proposals.reason: Literal singular 'he' conflicts with the plural joint arrival implied by the Chinese and the prior sentence naming both commanders.

proposals.before: After the war his Yu Battalion grew insubordinate; Li Bingheng was ordered to investigate, and Rong He was stripped of rank and punished.
proposals.after: After the war his Yu Battalion grew insubordinate; Li Bingheng was ordered to investigate, and Rong He was stripped of office and punished.
proposals.reason: '革職' is removal from office; 'stripped of rank' overstates the Chinese (literal correctly has stripped of office).

proposals.before: When the Xiang Army general Chen Ti arrived he again asked Liu Kunyi for a combined assault — again without result.
proposals.after: When the Xiang Army general Chen Shi arrived he again asked Liu Kunyi for a combined assault — again without result.
proposals.reason: 陳湜 is Chen Shi (湜 = shí); the packet English spelling Chen Ti is a clear name-reading error.

proposals.before: When the Hunan Army general Chen Ti arrived, he again asked Liu Kunyi to order a joint attack — again without success.
proposals.after: When the Hunan Army general Chen Shi arrived, he again asked Liu Kunyi to order a joint attack — again without success.
proposals.reason: 陳湜 is Chen Shi (湜 = shí); the literal English likewise misspells the personal name as Ti.

proposals.before: Song Qing and Yukun suffered defeats in succession and could no longer recover their strength.
proposals.after: Song Qing and Ma Yukun suffered defeats in succession and could no longer recover their strength.
proposals.reason: 玉昆 is Ma Yukun; the literal English drops the surname already supplied in the idiomatic rendering.

decisions.reason: 薦授千總 names the Green Standard company-grade office qianzong; 'battalion commander' over-ranks the title, and the proposed gloss is accurate.
Literal likewise misrenders 千總 as battalion commander; qianzong (company officer) matches the Qing grade.
予二等輕車都尉 is a Qing hereditary noble rank, not an Order of the Chariot of War; Light Chariot Commandant is the correct title.
Literal repeats the same 輕車都尉 error; second-class Light Chariot Commandant restores the hereditary rank.
行輩相若 marks shared generational/peer seniority, not official 品級 rank; replacing 'rank' with 'seniority' corrects the sense.
直趨鳳凰城 is the Japanese drive on Fengcheng after 戰失利; 退扼大高嶺 is the Qing fallback. The proposed agent split matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 直趨鳳凰城，退扼大高嶺

decisions.reason: Chinese names 李鴻章 in full; bare 'Hongzhang' drops the surname and leaves the agent ambiguous, while Li Hongzhang restores it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李鴻章別令薑桂題等守旅順

decisions.reason: 積功至都司 is the Qing grade dusí, conventionally major and below 參將; 'colonel' conflates distinct ranks.
Literal likewise over-ranks 都司 as colonel; major is the required Green Standard equivalent.
翼之出 uses 翼 as a verb 'to shield/flank and bring out'; 'escorted him out on both sides' misreads 翼 as a noun of sides.
有違言 means there were objections or discordant words over revising the Ili treaty; 'had words of breach' is an inaccurate calque.
諡誠勇，予建祠 bestows only the posthumous name Chengyong and a temple grant; 'Loyal and Brave' is an inserted gloss treated as part of the name.
既至 follows the joint charge of Zhang Shun and I Ketang'a; singular 'he' conflicts with that plural arrival, and 'they' matches 議.
革職治罪 is removal from office and punishment; 'stripped of rank' overstates 革職, while 'stripped of office' is exact.
陳湜 reads Chen Shi (湜 = shí); 'Chen Ti' is a wrong character reading, and the proposed spelling matches the Chinese.
Literal likewise misspells 陳湜 as Chen Ti; Chen Shi is the correct reading.
慶與玉昆 pairs Song Qing with Ma Yukun; once Qing is expanded to Song Qing, bare Yukun should carry the surname Ma already used in the idiomatic line.
